Updated: 2026-08-26

setwd("C:/MisLocalFiles/Github/HBSC/scripts")

library(purrr)

Dataset Overview


hbsc2018 <- read_delim(paste0(project_folder,
                                  "/data/raw/HBSC2018OAed1.1.csv"),
                       delim = ";",
                       na = c("", " "))
# working copy
dat <- hbsc2018

File has the following rows and columns:


dim(hbsc2018)
[1] 244097    120

Pretty much all columns have missing values so need to address later. Though it seems much of the variables I will care about don’t have much.


na_cnts <- data.frame(
  variable = names(dat),
  na_count = sapply(dat, function(x) sum(is.na(x)))
)

row.names(na_cnts) <- NULL

na_cnts <- na_cnts %>%
  mutate(na_pct = round(100 * na_count / nrow(dat),1)) %>%
  arrange(desc(na_count))

print(na_cnts)

Variables to Predict

lifesat

Q: Here is a picture of a ladder. The top of the ladder “10” is the best possible life for you and the bottom “0” is the worst possible life for you. In general, where on the ladder do you feel you stand at the moment? A: 0-10


ggplot(dat, aes(y = factor(lifesat))) +
  geom_bar(fill = "steelblue") +
  labs(
    y = "lifesat",
    x = "n"
    ) +
  theme_minimal()

lifesat is dichotomized for modeling as lifesat_low:


dat <- dat %>%
  mutate(
    lifesat_low = case_when(
      between(lifesat, 0, 5) ~ 1,
      between(lifesat, 6, 10) ~ 0,
      TRUE ~ NA))

(mental) health complaints

There are 8 variables for this that reply to a question like: In the last 6 months: how often have you had the following….? And the answers goes from 1 About every day to 5 Rarely or never. The 8 variables are: headache, stomachache, backache, dizzy, feellow, irritable, nervous, sleepdificulty.

Their distributions look like this:


vars_health_complaints <- c("headache", "stomachache", "backache", "dizzy",
          "feellow", "irritable", "nervous", "sleepdificulty")

plot_list <- map(vars_health_complaints, function(v) {
  ggplot(dat, aes(y = factor(.data[[v]]))) +
    geom_bar(fill = "steelblue") +
    coord_flip() +
    labs(
      y = v,
      x = "n"
    ) +
    theme_minimal()
})

wrap_plots(plot_list, ncol = 2)

These variables are then recoded to a binary where it flags if the complaint occurs more than once per week (1 or 2).


dat <- dat %>%
  mutate(
    headache_frequent = ifelse(headache <= 2, 1, 0),
    stomachache_frequent = ifelse(stomachache <= 2, 1, 0),
    backache_frequent = ifelse(backache <= 2, 1, 0),
    dizzy_frequent = ifelse(dizzy <= 2, 1, 0),
    feellow_frequent = ifelse(feellow <= 2, 1, 0),
    irritable_frequent = ifelse(irritable <= 2, 1, 0),
    nervous_frequent = ifelse(nervous <= 2, 1, 0),
    sleepdificulty_frequent = ifelse(sleepdificulty <= 2, 1, 0)
  )

The recoded variables look like this:


vars_health_complaints_frequent <- paste0(vars_health_complaints,

for (i in seq_along(vars_health_complaints)) {
  cat("\n\n###", vars_health_complaints[i], "x", vars_health_complaints_frequent[i], "\n")
  print(table(dat[[vars_health_complaints[i]]], dat[[vars_health_complaints_frequent[i]]], useNA = "always"))
}

The frequency of complaints is then added to calculate one sum for physical and one for mental. If the sum is 2 or more then it is determined that there is a health issue. Most papers do it for psycosomatic (all 8 vars) but I will focus on the 4 mental ones. Still, I include both vars in case.


dat <- dat %>%
  # add the frequency of complaints
  mutate(mental_complaints_sum = feellow_frequent +
                           irritable_frequent +
                           nervous_frequent +
                           sleepdificulty_frequent,
         physical_complaints_sum = headache_frequent +
                           stomachache_frequent +
                           backache_frequent + 
                           dizzy_frequent
  ) %>%
  # derive index based on sum
  mutate(mental_complaintsY = ifelse(mental_complaints_sum >=2, 1, 0),
         health_complaintsY = ifelse((mental_complaints_sum + physical_complaints_sum) >=2, 1, 0)
      ) 

cat("\n\n### mental_complaintsY x mental_complaints_sum\n")

The Predictors

Problematic social media use (PMSU)

PMSU are the main variables of interest. There are 9 of them: emcsocmed1 to emcsocmed9. The prequestion for all of them is: We are interested in your experiences with social media. The term social media refers to social network sites (e.g. Facebook, [add other local examples]) and instant messengers (e.g. [insert local examples], WhatsApp, Snapchat, Facebook messenger). During the past year, have you…. Please tick one box for each line.

The possible answers are 1 (no) and 2 (yes). Also those with 99 mean Missing due to skip pattern.

The topic of each question is:


questions <- data.frame(
  item = c(
    "emcsocmed1","emcsocmed2","emcsocmed3","emcsocmed4",
    "emcsocmed5","emcsocmed6","emcsocmed7","emcsocmed8","emcsocmed9"
  ),
  topic = c(
    "Social media: I can't think of anything else",
    "Social media: Dissatisfied cause want to spend more time",
    "Social media: Felt bad cause want to play",
    "Social media: Failed to spend less time",
    "Social media: Neglected other activities",
    "Social media: Had arguments because of use",
    "Social media: Lied about amount of time spent",
    "Social media: Use it to escape from negative feelings",
    "Social media: Conflict with family because of use"
  )
)

Since I need to get a sum of them I will recode them from 1/2 to 0/1.These are the distributions of the answers. I put the 99 as NA - is that correct?

The recoding looks like this:


# recode emcsocmed to 0/1 from 1/2
recode_emcsocmed <- function(old_col){
  new_col <- case_when(
    old_col == 1 ~ 0,
    old_col == 2 ~ 1,
    TRUE ~ NA #99?
  )
  return(new_col)
}

dat <- dat %>%
  mutate(emcsocmed1_r = recode_emcsocmed(emcsocmed1),
         emcsocmed2_r = recode_emcsocmed(emcsocmed2),
         emcsocmed3_r = recode_emcsocmed(emcsocmed3),
         emcsocmed4_r = recode_emcsocmed(emcsocmed4),
         emcsocmed5_r = recode_emcsocmed(emcsocmed5),
         emcsocmed6_r = recode_emcsocmed(emcsocmed6),
         emcsocmed7_r = recode_emcsocmed(emcsocmed7),
         emcsocmed8_r = recode_emcsocmed(emcsocmed8),
         emcsocmed9_r = recode_emcsocmed(emcsocmed9)
         ) 

vars <- paste0("emcsocmed", 1:9)

for (v in vars) {
  cat("## Table for", v)
  print(table(dat[[v]], dat[[paste0(v, "_r")]], useNA = "always"))
  cat("\n\n")
}

PMSU variables are then combined so output is represented in one variable, instead of 9. I will do 2 versions: a) Yes/No where Y(6-9) and N(0-5) b) H/M/L where H(6-9), M(2-5) and L(0-1)

The distribution of PMSU categorized is:


vars_emcsocmed <- paste0("emcsocmed", 1:9)
vars_emcsocmed_r <- paste0("emcsocmed", 1:9, "_r")

dat <- dat %>%
  mutate(emcsocmed_sum = rowSums(dat[,vars_emcsocmed_r])) %>%
  mutate(
    pmsu_yn = case_when(
      between(emcsocmed_sum,6,9) ~ 1,
      between(emcsocmed_sum,0,5) ~ 0,
      TRUE ~ NA
    ),
    pmsu_lmh = case_when(
      between(emcsocmed_sum,6,9) ~ "High",
      between(emcsocmed_sum,2,5) ~ "Med",
      between(emcsocmed_sum,0,1) ~ "Low",
      TRUE ~ NA
    )
  )

cat("## Table for emcsocmed_sum x pmsu_yn")

Family Support

There are 4 of them. The question starts with: We are interested in how you feel about the following statements. Please show how much you agree or disagree with each one. Please tick one box for each line.

The options to answer go from 1 Very strongly disagree to 7 Very strongly agree. The 4 questions are:


family_items <- data.frame(
  item = c(
    "famhelp",
    "famsup",
    "famtalk",
    "famclose"
  ),
  topic = c(
    "Family tries to help",
    "Get emotional help from family",
    "Talk about problems with family",
    "Feel close to family"
  )
)

kable(family_items) #, caption = "Family Support Items")
item topic
famhelp Family tries to help
famsup Get emotional help from family
famtalk Talk about problems with family
famclose Feel close to family 
NA

These variables are then combined to create a categorical predictor. For now, I will keep two options like I did for PMSU but will select only one when modeling. These are:
a) H/L based on avg of 4 vars. L if [1,5.5) and H if [5.5, 7]
b) H/M/L based on sum of 4 vars. L if 4-11, M if 12-19, H if 20-28.


vars_family_support <- c("famhelp", "famsup", "famtalk", "famdec")

dat <- dat %>%
   mutate(family_support_avg = rowMeans(dat[,vars_family_support]),
          family_support_sum = rowSums(dat[,vars_family_support])
          ) %>%
   mutate(family_support_high = case_when(
            family_support_avg >= 1 & family_support_avg < 5.5 ~ 0,
            family_support_avg >= 5.5 & family_support_avg <= 7 ~ 1,
            TRUE ~ NA)) %>%
   mutate(family_support_hml = case_when(
            family_support_sum >= 4 & family_support_sum <= 11 ~ "Low",
            family_support_sum >= 12 & family_support_sum <= 19 ~ "Med",
            family_support_sum >= 20 & family_support_sum <= 28 ~ "High",
            TRUE ~ NA))

Their counts after recoding are:

Friends (Peer) Support

There are 4 friends support questions. The questions start with: We are interested in how you feel about the following statements. Please show how much you agree or disagree with each one. Please tick one box for each line.

The answers range from 1 Very strongly disagree to 7 Very strongly agree.

friend_items <- data.frame(
  item = c(
    "friendhelp",
    "friendcounton",
    "friendshare",
    "friendtalk"
  ),
  topic = c(
    "My friends really try to help me",
    "I can count on my friends when things go wrong",
    "I have friends with whom I can share my joys and sorrows",
    "I can talk about my problems with my friends"
  )
)

kable(friend_items)
item topic
friendhelp My friends really try to help me
friendcounton I can count on my friends when things go wrong
friendshare I have friends with whom I can share my joys and sorrows
friendtalk I can talk about my problems with my friends 
NA

These variables are then combined to create a categorical predictor. For now, I will keep two options like I did for family but will select only one when modeling. These are:
a) H/L based on avg of 4 vars. L if [1,5.5) and H if [5.5, 7]
b) H/M/L based on sum of 4 vars. L if 4-11, M if 12-19, H if 20-28.


vars_friends_support <- c("friendhelp", "friendcounton", "friendshare", "friendtalk")
# recode friends/peer support as yn and hml
dat <- dat %>%
  mutate(friends_support_avg = rowMeans(dat[,vars_friends_support]),
         friends_support_sum = rowSums(dat[,vars_friends_support])
  ) %>%
  mutate(friends_support_high = case_when(
    friends_support_avg >= 1 & friends_support_avg < 5.5 ~ 0,
    friends_support_avg >= 5.5 & friends_support_avg <= 7 ~ 1,
    TRUE ~ NA)) %>%
  mutate(friends_support_hml = case_when(
    friends_support_sum >= 4 & friends_support_sum <= 11 ~ "Low",
    friends_support_sum >= 12 & friends_support_sum <= 19 ~ "Med",
    friends_support_sum >= 20 & friends_support_sum <= 28 ~ "High",
    TRUE ~ NA))

School support

This metric is a combination of multiple questions from 2 categories: teacher acceptance and classmates acceptance. The answers to these questions go from 1 (strong agree) to 5 (strong disagree).

The questions are:


school_items <- data.frame(
  category = c("teacher", "teacher", "teacher",
               "classmates", "classmates", "classmates"),
  item = c("teacheraccept",
           "teachercare",
           "teachertrust",
           "studtogether",
           "studhelpful",
           "studaccept"),
  topic = c("Teacher accepts me",
            "Teacher cares about me",
            "Feel trust in teacher",
            "Students enjoy being together",
            "Students kind and helpful",
            "Students accept me")
)

kable(school_items)

The scales of these variables is reversed so 1 is negative and 5 is the most positive. Then an arithmetic average is calculated for teacher and students. The based on this average a high/low support is calculated for each with 4 being the threshold.


# recodes from 1-5 to 0-4 (06-italy)
recode_school_vars <- function(old_values){
  
  new_values <- case_when(
    old_values == 5 ~ 1,
    old_values == 4 ~ 2,
    old_values == 3 ~ 3,
    old_values == 2 ~ 4,
    old_values == 1 ~ 5,
    TRUE ~ NA
  )
  
  return(new_values)
  
}

dat <- dat %>%
  # recode they can be added
  mutate(teacheraccept_r = recode_school_vars(teacheraccept),
         teachercare_r = recode_school_vars(teachercare),
         teachertrust_r = recode_school_vars(teachertrust),
         studtogether_r = recode_school_vars(studtogether),
         studhelpful_r = recode_school_vars(studhelpful),
         studaccept_r = recode_school_vars(studaccept)
         ) %>%
  # derive avg by teacher/student
  mutate(teacher_support_avg = (teacheraccept_r 
                               + teachercare_r
                               + teachertrust_r) / 3,
         student_support_avg = (studtogether_r
                                + studhelpful_r
                                + studaccept_r) / 3,
         # just for fun combine and try
         school_support_avg = (teacheraccept_r 
                                + teachercare_r
                                + teachertrust_r
                                + studtogether_r
                                + studhelpful_r
                                + studaccept_r) / 6,
         ) %>%
  # derive support yn based on hbsc
  mutate(
    teacher_support_high = case_when(
      teacher_support_avg >= 4 ~ 1,
      teacher_support_avg < 4 ~ 0,
      TRUE ~ NA),
      student_support_high = case_when(
        student_support_avg >= 4 ~ 1,
        student_support_avg < 4 ~ 0,
        TRUE ~ NA),
      school_support_high = case_when(
        school_support_avg >= 4 ~ 1,
        school_support_avg < 4 ~ 0,
      TRUE ~ NA)
  )

The recoding of each var is:


vars_school <- c("teacheraccept",
           "teachercare",
           "teachertrust",
           "studtogether",
           "studhelpful",
           "studaccept")

vars_school_r <- paste0(vars_school,
                        "_r")

for (i in seq_along(vars_school)) {
  cat("\n\n###", vars_school[i], "x", vars_school_r[i], "\n")
  print(table(dat[[vars_school[i]]], dat[[vars_school_r[i]]], useNA = "always"))
}

Continuos Online Communications

This category measures how how often young person communicate online with 4 types of people in their life. Preamble of question is: How often do you have ONLINE contact with the following people? Answers range from 1 (NA or don’t know) to 6 (almost all of the time).

Variable Description
emconlfreq1 Online contact with close friends
emconlfreq2 Online contact with larger friend group
emconlfreq3 Online contact with online friends
emconlfreq4 Online contact with other

I combine this into one dichotomized and adopt the HBSC definition of yes if any of the variables is 6.


dat <- dat %>%
  mutate(emconlfreqYes = case_when(
    (emconlfreq1 == 6 | emconlfreq2 == 6 | emconlfreq3 == 6 | emconlfreq4 == 6) ~ 1,
    (!is.na(emconlfreq1) | !is.na(emconlfreq2) | !is.na(emconlfreq3) | !is.na(emconlfreq4)) ~ 0,
    TRUE ~ NA
  ))
